setup: 41 real memory records; 5 query types (multi, KV, DSH, architecture, next priorities); budgets 1200/1800/2400; learnedTopK 1/4/8/16; rule vs hybrid; key-record coverage measured.
findings: Coverage is non-monotonic in budget/topK: the multi query hits 3/4 key records at 1200-1800/topK8 but 0/4 at 2400/topK8 because large top candidates consume the budget and fewer pages fit.

KV key record is selected at all tested budgets for hybrid; DSH is hit at 1200 and 1800/topK4-8 but missed at 2400; architecture is hit only at specific 1800/2400 configurations; next-priorities generally hit.
Returned tokens exceed budget by ~1-8% because the stable prefix is not included in the page budget.
Hybrid can select fewer pages than rule when learned top candidates are large; topK alone is not budget-aware.
Rule already includes some key records by chronology, so coverage comparison must be query-specific.
Actual active config currently set to 1800/topK8 rather than 2400/topK8 based on this matrix.
optimizationDirections: Budget-aware reranking: score per token, cap/truncate huge pages, and enforce total window budget including prefix.
Core-fact tier: guarantee architecture/KV/DSH/priorities summary records via pinned or always-include summary pages.
Diversity/coverage constraints for learnedTopK: avoid adding near-duplicate huge pages that evict key short records.
Query routing / semantic reranker: lexical overlap is weak for architecture and cross-topic queries; use BGE cross-encoder or query-type routing.
Multi-query benchmark with human-verified answers; current matrix is key-record coverage, not answer quality.
Validate non-monotonic behavior with real DSH trace before defaulting hybrid.
caveats: Key-record coverage is a proxy, not answer correctness.
One dataset/config family; no production traffic.
Token estimates include prefix; budget semantics need clarification.
